transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-09
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ethan Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Ana Torres (KestrelGrid Partnerships), Darren Liu (Infra Lead), Sanjay Patel (CTO), Maya R. (Procurement), Oliver (Integrator)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
Redwood intro, talk about host/dedicated/private, edge GPU, reseller, security and benchmark. Customer concerned about latency and on-prem gating and marketplace revenue share.

Topics: integration patterns, private VPC, GPU SKUs, KV cache/latency, reselling/marketplace, pilot scope, timelines, procurement constraints.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side — Ethan Rivera, AE. With me: Priya, our SE, and Jamal in solutions. How about you folks?
[00:08] Ana (KestrelGrid): Hey, Ana here. We're excited to chat — partnership lead at KestrelGrid. Darren and Sanjay are on from infra. Maya from procurement. Oliver is our SI lead.
[00:13] Ethan: Awesome. Goal today is discovery — understand your use cases for edge and SI integrations, any GPU constraints, and see where Redwood fits as a hosted, dedicated, or private option. Also talk about partner/reseller flow.
[00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Quick technical intro — Redwood serves models in three modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved clusters, and private VPC/on-prem. We do batching, KV cache, quantization support, and can route by policy.
[00:32] Darren (KestrelGrid): Right. At KestrelGrid we're building an edge gateway for telco customers. We run hybrid clusters — some on cloud GPUs, some on colocation racks. Main concern is deterministic latency at the edge and secure tenancy.
[00:45] Sanjay (CTO): Also reseller: we want to package Redwood inference into our SI offering and potentially list on our partner marketplace. Need clarity on commercial splits and how updates/rollouts work for private deployments.
[00:58] Ethan: Good flags. On private deployments we can ship a customer-managed control plane with integrations to KMS/HSM, and provide audit logs and RBAC. Rollouts are controlled via version pinning and canary policies.
[01:12] Oliver (Integrator): A quick practical Q — how does KV cache behave across intermittent networks at the edge? We often have flaky WANs.
[01:20] Priya: Yeah, so our KV cache is local to the serving node; we support prefix caching as well as proactive warmers. For flaky networks, we recommend local snapshots and a fallback to a smaller quantized variant. There can be some staleness but it keeps latency bounded.
[01:38] Darren: And what about GPU SKUs? We have A100s in colo and some T4-equivalents at edge racks. Need to know compatibility and perf delta.
[01:47] Priya: We typically validate per SKU. A100 gives best throughput, T4/RTX-class plus quantization works for lower-latency low-cost profiles. We'll produce a perf profile mapping during the benchmark.
[02:01] Ana: For the partner model: do you support reseller revenue share or marketplace listing? Our legal needs to see an MSA stub.
[02:09] Ethan: Yes, we have reseller/partner programs — we can share a marketplace term sheet. For enterprise private deals, there's a platform license plus per-node/min monthly fee. We'll send a term sheet and sample MSA.
[02:22] Maya (Procurement): Important: we need SOC2 attestation, ISO27001, and ability to route logs into our SIEM. Also need to see encryption at rest with KMS.
[02:32] Jamal (Redwood): We can provide SOC2 Type II, ISO artifacts, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key control. For logs, we support secure log forwarding and long-term retention as an add-on.
[02:44] Sanjay: Latency SLOs — can you commit to p95 numbers for typical seq lengths? Our SLAs with telco customers are strict.
[02:53] Priya: We'll need a benchmark run with your workloads to commit. Typically on A100s we can hit p95s under X ms for 512 tokens but it's workload-dependent. We'll plan a benchmarking session with your sample prompts to produce SLO targets.
[03:09] Darren: What about cold-starts across microservices? Our workloads have lots of short-lived connections.
[03:15] Priya: Continuous batching and warm pools help. We also support burst pools to handle spikes. There's a tradeoff with cost; we'll show cost-per-token curves in the bench report.
[03:28] Ana: On timelines — if we want to pilot by Q1, what does enablement look like? Training, docs, joint go-to-market?
[03:36] Ethan: Typical partner enablement: 1) technical kickoff, 2) pilot/benchmark, 3) solution integration and packaging for your marketplace, 4) joint GTM assets. We can aim for a pilot in early Jan if we start paperwork now.
[03:48] Maya: Procurement needs lead times for PO cycles — may be 6 weeks. We'll work the calendar.
[03:53] Oliver: A little more on the integration: we'll need a deployment pattern for on-prem customers where network egress is restricted. Does Redwood support fully air-gapped or semi-air-gapped installs?
[04:04] Jamal: We have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments, though it requires additional site validation. Semi-air-gapped with outbound to an update mirror is also supported.
[04:17] Sanjay: How do updates work for private installs? We cannot have surprise changes.
[04:22] Priya: Updates are controlled; customers can pin versions and apply canary rollouts. For private, we hand over update artifacts and a validated upgrade plan.
[04:30] Darren: Any references for SI partnerships where you've done reseller integrations? We want case studies.
[04:35] Ethan: We'll share partner success stories and a two-page enablement checklist. One minor note — some auto transcribe bits are off: Redwood product names sometimes show as "Redwho?" in older docs, ignore that.
[04:46] Ana: (laughs) okay that explains some old slides.
[04:50] Priya: On the benchmarking plan: we'll need your sample request patterns, token distributions, and target QPS. Also list of SKUs you can provide in the pilot.
[04:59] Darren: I'll send cluster topology, current GPU inventory, and expected peak patterns. Expect that by Wednesday.
[05:05] Ethan: Great. For pilot success criteria, let's align: 1) meet p95 latency target for the chosen SKU, 2) demonstrate stable KV cache behavior for intermittent networks, 3) document cost per 1M tokens at target perf.
[05:19] Sanjay: Agreed. Also need security checklist completion.
[05:23] Maya: On commercial side: can you provide indicative pricing ranges for dedicated pools vs private installs? We need this for preliminary modeling.
[05:31] Ethan: We'll provide a pricing grid — hosted per-token, dedicated reserved monthly, and private platform license ranges. Exact numbers are for the term sheet.
[05:39] Oliver: Any gotchas for telco/regulatory environments? Data residency and packet inspection concerns?
[05:44] Jamal: We support region pinning and can disable telemetry. For deeper packet inspection concerns, we work with customers on netflow-only exports and detailed audit logs.
[05:55] Ana: Last thing — rollout: can Redwood co-market with us on the partner marketplace listing? We want joint collateral.
[06:01] Ethan: Yes — joint listing, co-branded collateral, and technical enablement. We'll loop in partner marketing after legal is aligned.
[06:09] Darren: Ok that covers it for me.
[06:12] Ethan: Quick recap of next steps: we will send the reseller term sheet and MSA stub, Priya will draft the benchmarking plan, KestrelGrid to send cluster details, and procurement will start review. We schedule the benchmark session for the week of 2027-12-20 if that works.
[06:29] Ana: Works for us. Thanks all.
[06:32] Ethan: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email with links to the security pack and the partner onboarding doc.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcript quality: medium — multiple speaker overlaps, some proper nouns mis-transcribed (e.g., KMS sometimes appears as "KMSs"), and timestamps approximate.
